To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface free energy values of polyurethane elastomer coatings depend on the chemical structure of the polyol used in the synthesis of the prepolymer and that of the chain extender.
it was possible to obtain coatings with the desired SFE values by the selection of the appropriate substrates, as well as by the choice of the appropriate polyurethane raw material.
the surface free energy of polyurethane coatings can be predicted from their chemical structure and that this prediction can be used to design coatings with desired properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of predicting the SFE of the polyurethane coatings obtained from various polyols, isocyanates, and extenders.
the possibility of predicting the surface free energy values of the polyurethane coatings by the selection of the raw materials used for their production.
the possibility of obtaining polyurethane coatings of the appropriate surface energy by selection of the appropriate raw materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SFE of the investigated coatings depends on the type and amount of the chain extender and the type of the polyurethane prepolymers.
it is not possible to predict the SFE values of polyurethane coatings on the basis of the chemical structure of the polyurethane raw material only.
the surface free energy of the polyurethane coats depends mainly on the chemical structure of the polyurethanes used as a coating material and the type of substrate used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SFE values of coatings can be predicted with a satisfactory precision, using empirical correlations based on the values of the mole fractions of structural fragments responsible for the polar and dispersive interactions within the polymer chain.
the use of HO-tertiaries amines as the chain extenders is essential to obtain hydrophilic coatings, while the use of diols is necessary to achieve hydrophobic ones.

it is possible by using the 1H N MR method and the Owens–Wendr method, to determine the surface free energy of polyurethane elastomer coatings, and to predict their values by using the empirical equations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface free energy of polyurethane coatings can be controlled by selection of appropriate polyol type, diisocyanide type, and chain extender.
the surface energy of polyurethane coatings can be predicted based on the chemical structure of polyurethane chains.
the surface free energy values of polyurethane coatings can be controlled in a wide range, by the appropriate selection of the raw materials used for their synthesis.
